title: The Man Who Put His Head in a Particle Accelerator: The Full Case of Anatoli Bugorski
description:
Case 013, the full case file. In 1978 Anatoli Bugorski was a physicist at the Institute for High Energy Physics in Protvino, home of the U-70 synchrotron, then the largest particle accelerator in the Soviet Union. He went to check a piece of equipment that was not working. A safety mechanism had failed (by one account, warning lights had been switched off for an earlier experiment and not switched back on) and the proton beam was still running when he leaned in. It went in at the back of his head and came out by the left side of his nose. He reportedly saw a flash 'brighter than a thousand suns' and felt no pain. He finished his work and at first told nobody. Then the left side of his face swelled up, and he was taken to a clinic in Moscow, where doctors expected him to die.

He lived. The usual explanation is that the beam was narrow, so the dose ran along one thin line through his head and not through his whole body. He lost the hearing in his left ear, the left half of his face became paralysed and he has had seizures, but he completed his doctorate and went back to work at the same institute, later coordinating experiments on the same accelerator. The story was not public for about a decade. In 1996 he applied for disability status and was turned down. Rook didn't believe it either.

About the numbers: sources give different figures for the dose. The film quotes one set (about 2,000 gray where the beam entered and 3,000 where it left, against roughly 5 gray as a whole-body dose that can kill) and says so; other accounts give 200,000 to 300,000 roentgens, or simply 'hundreds of times a lethal dose'. Sources also differ on the date: most give 13 July 1978, one gives June.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The road, gate, ring seen from the air, tunnel, corridor, control room, van, clinic, study and office in the film are generic low-poly sets, not models of the real places, machines or vehicles; the extra people (operators, doctors, a clerk) are stand-ins and not likenesses; and the cards, calendar leaves, gauge, form and diagrams are drawings made for it, not real documents or medical images. A proton beam inside an accelerator is not visible; the film draws it as a line of light so the story can be followed. His seizures are not depicted, only a man who has had to sit down. This is not safety guidance for any real facility.

source_notes: IMPORTANT, read before making this public: no web page could be opened in this run (15 Nov 2026). Every fetch (Wikipedia 'Anatoli Bugorski' and 'U-70 (synchrotron)', Wired 1997, Discover, Amusing Planet, Big Think, Gizmodo, Atlas Obscura, IFLScience) was refused with 'PROVENANCE_REQUIRED: the permission request for this URL was not answered in time', because nobody was there to approve it; web search returned titles and links only, no text. No archive, mirror or other route was used. So this film adds NO fact from new reading. Everything in it comes from what the Short's run read and recorded earlier the same day in episodes/r013-bugorski/episode.json (source_notes), and the five sources listed are the five pages that run read. For that reason the episode is shipped as 'ready' (private), not 'approved'. Facts the Short already narrated stand as documented there (1978, physicist at the institute in Protvino, the U-70 as the biggest accelerator in the Soviet Union, checking faulty equipment, a failed safety mechanism, in at the back of the head and out by the nose, the flash 'brighter than a thousand suns' by his account, no pain, the swollen left side of the face, the Moscow clinic where doctors expected him to die, 'hundreds of times a lethal dose by some estimates', hearing lost in the left ear, the left half of the face paralysed, the doctorate, back to work at the same accelerator). Facts added by the long version, each with what the Short's notes record for it: (1) The Institute for High Energy Physics and the name U-70, a synchrotron: all five pages. (2) The date: 13 July 1978 in Discover, Gizmodo, Big Think and Amusing Planet, 3 June 1978 in Wikipedia; narrated as 'Most accounts say July the thirteenth. One says June.' (3) Warning lights switched off for an earlier experiment and not switched back on: Amusing Planet only, so narrated as 'by one account'. (4) Out by the LEFT side of the nose: Wikipedia. (5) He finished his work and at first told nobody: Wikipedia and Amusing Planet. (6) Dose of about 2,000 gray on entry and 3,000 on exit, against roughly 5 gray as a lethal whole-body dose: Discover and Gizmodo; Wikipedia gives 200,000 to 300,000 roentgens and Amusing Planet notes that sources disagree, so the narration says 'one set of figures' and 'the sources don't agree on the exact number'. (7) He has had seizures: Discover, Gizmodo, Wikipedia, Amusing Planet. (8) Later a coordinator of experiments on the same accelerator: Wikipedia only. The next three are in the Short's notes WITHOUT a named page, and are the ones to check first: (9) the narrow beam, so a local dose along its path and not a whole-body dose, 'the usual explanation for his survival'; (10) 'the decade of secrecy' (narrated as 'for about a decade, almost none of this is public'); (11) 'his unsuccessful 1996 application for disability status' (narrated as 'he applies for disability status. He is turned down'; no reason for the refusal is given because none is recorded). Also general knowledge and not a sourced fact: a proton beam inside an accelerator cannot be seen. Deliberately left out because nothing recorded supports them in enough detail: his age, his birth date, the beam energy, how he got to Moscow (the van is a generic stand-in), how long he was in the clinic, what kind of seizures, his fatigue, his family, and anything after 1996. Rook's lines about himself ('I would have been heard in Moscow', 'I have no joke for that', the advice about a dark warning lamp) are the host's comments, not facts about the case.

quality_gate.method: Reviewed in three rounds with fixes after each. Round 1, the 16:9 3D contact sheet (68 stills, three parts): the roadside shot was black (camera inside a tree; the near verge was cleared), the last lamp shot was black (camera through a wall), the reused work shot looked out from inside a magnet, Rook was out of frame in the lever shot and hidden behind the counter in the cabinet shot, the counter hid the clerk (lowered), the close-up of the swollen face looked at the top of his head, Rook was seen only from behind at the pipe (camera moved to look through the gap at him) and was too far away in the 'drawn in' shot, the plinth built for one shot showed in the others (now parked), the corridor was washed out. Round 2, spot frames of the 23 restaged shots, composited stills of all 83 shots with captions, HUD, inserts and overlays, and the thumbnail: the thumbnail was rebuilt twice (Rook was out of frame and the beam was a fat white bar that burned out his face; the hook was cut from six words to four and pulled in from the edge), an empty calendar label crashed the compositor, two labels sat too near the captions, Rook stood too low in the office shot. Round 3, a full-length low-resolution rehearsal (384x216, 4 samples, every 3D frame) composited at 1920x1080 with sound, and a late frame of every shot pulled from it: the dose sequence ran behind the words (the two dose cards now come when the figures are spoken), the drawing of 'not the whole body' had a strike-through that read as the beam going through the body (removed; the figure is plain blue), two stamps covered a note and a caption (moved). The changed shots were rendered again and the film composited again. Both rehearsals PASSED the automated gate locally; the second: 83 shots, mean 1.99 s, longest 3.58 s, loudness -15.2 LUFS, voice 12.3 dB over the bed, host in 40/83 shots (48%), closest match to an earlier episode 0.78. By rule: every 3D kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D and every flat kind in scenes.SHOTS, HOST lists the kinds where Rook is placed, no kind is used more than three times or twice in a row, the first shot is 1.6 s with an impact sound at its start, and the repository tests pass. Audio was measured, not listened to. The fingerprint file the local gate wrote was deleted, not committed. The full-resolution render and the real gate run in the cloud.
quality_gate.checked: Nothing graphic is shown (a bandage, a swollen cheek, a man sitting down with his eyes shut for the seizures); the jokes stop from the swelling to the wait, and again for the 1996 refusal; no lettering, emblem, flag or real document appears in the 3D sets, the van has no markings, and the cards are labelled drawings. The dose figures on screen are labelled 'one set of figures' and the gauge carries none.
quality_gate.why_ready_not_approved: No source page could be opened in this run, so the facts the long version adds were not re-read; three of them (the narrow-beam explanation, the decade of secrecy, the 1996 refusal) are recorded in the Short's notes without a named page.
